name: I Am Sober
one_liner: Sobriety tracker: count sober days and money saved, make a daily pledge, and post in a peer community. Free, with paid Sober Plus.
best_for: People in recovery who want a daily tracker and pledge for motivation
People cutting out alcohol, drugs or another habit who like seeing streaks and money saved
People who find support in an online peer community
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who may need medical detox or supervised withdrawal: stopping alcohol or some drugs suddenly can be dangerous
People who want treatment, counseling or medication: it is a tracker and peer community only
short_description: A free sobriety-tracking app with daily pledges, milestones and a peer community, plus an optional Sober Plus subscription.
long_description: I Am Sober counts your time sober from alcohol, drugs, smoking or other habits, tracks money saved and milestones, and asks you to make a pledge each morning and reflect each evening. It has a peer community where members share stories and support, plus journaling and motivation content. The core tracker and community are free; Sober Plus, an optional in-app subscription, adds workbook activities and challenges, tracking more than one addiction, creating private groups, an app lock and cloud backup. Community posts are public. It is popular and often recommended by addiction counselors, but we found no published study of whether it helps people stay sober. It is a support tool and doesn't offer treatment or medical care.
patient_summary: I Am Sober tracks your sober days, celebrates milestones and asks you to commit to staying sober each day, with a peer community for support. The tracker and community are free; Sober Plus is an optional paid upgrade. It works best alongside treatment, a support group or counseling.

pricing.notes: Sobriety counter, daily pledge and community are free. Sober Plus is optional with a 7-day trial; I Am Sober doesn't publish its price, and the figures shown come from 2026 reviews and vary by store and region (some listings show different prices). Check the price in the app.

privacy.notes: Policy says data is shared only with providers needed to run the service (e.g. AWS, Google Analytics, PostHog, RevenueCat) or when required by law. Delete your account in Settings > Account. Community posts are public.

faqs.q: Is I Am Sober effective for staying sober?
faqs.a: Many users find the daily pledge system and milestone tracking helpful for maintaining motivation in recovery. The app is a support tool, not a treatment. It works best as part of a broader recovery plan that may include therapy, support groups, or other treatment.

faqs.q: What can I track with I Am Sober?
faqs.a: You can track sobriety from any substance or behavior including alcohol, drugs, smoking, gambling, or anything else. The app counts your sober time, money saved, milestones reached, and includes a journal for reflection.

faqs.q: Is the I Am Sober community anonymous?
faqs.a: Yes. You can choose any username and don't need to share identifying information. The community is moderated and focused on support and encouragement.

faqs.q: Can I Am Sober replace AA or treatment?
faqs.a: I Am Sober is a supplementary tool, not a replacement for treatment, therapy, or support groups like AA. It works well alongside these other supports to provide daily motivation and tracking.

primary_uses: Daily sobriety pledge and evening check-in
